clue.text: Churchwarden possibly married mother in the afternoon

parts.note: a churchwarden is a long-stemmed clay pipe, so this is an example of a pipe
MA is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A church official, perhaps newly wed, has his mother round for the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: A churchwarden here is not a parish officer but a long clay tobacco pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Old military signallers' phonetic alphabet spoke p.m. as 'pip emma', so it names the hours after noon.

clue.text: Distressing father almost completely

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: almost means the phrase stops one letter short

parts.note: in full means completely

explanation.surface: A father who is nearly completely upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that causes pain or upset is hurtful and distressing.

clue.text: Internet-age ploy adjusted work capacity based on position

indicators.note: adjusted says the letters of the phrase are altered into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A modern online tactic was tweaked.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics, stored energy depends on position, as in a raised weight able to do work.

clue.text: Queen is allowed to imprison republican

indicators.note: imprison says the word for allowed holds the letter inside

parts.note: may means is permitted

explanation.surface: A queen has the right to lock up a republican, the old royal grudge.
explanation.definitionFit: Several English and Scottish queens bore this name, such as Mary Tudor.

clue.text: Bloomer once more cut reduced funds

indicators.note: cut says the final letter of the first phrase is chopped

parts.note: anew means once more

indicators.note: reduced trims the last letter off the word for funds

parts.note: money means funds

explanation.surface: Someone's funds have been cut back yet again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder or loaf but means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that blooms is a flowerer, and the windflower is a garden flower.

clue.text: A king enters without a consort (still sleeping)

indicators.note: enters says the following pair of letters goes inside the word for unmarried

parts.note: having no spouse means unwed
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch with no spouse is pictured lying in, still asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not yet roused from slumber has not been woken; the word is an old-fashioned past participle form.

clue.text: Aristocratic groom is not put away

parts.note: U denotes upper-class usage, as in the U and non-U distinction
to groom is to tidy or neaten

explanation.surface: A posh bridegroom has not been locked away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put away' means eaten, as in putting away a large meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has not been consumed has not been put away in the slang sense of scoffed.

clue.text: Extended line taken from Irish writer

indicators.note: taken from says a letter is removed from the writer's name

parts.note: Oscar Wilde was an Irish writer

explanation.surface: A lengthy line lifted from an Irish author.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extended across a big span is broad or far-reaching.

clue.text: Oak family over rising mist, lifting around natural resources

indicators.note: over places this piece above the next in a down clue

parts.note: kin are family

indicators.note: rising means the word is read upwards in this down entry

parts.note: fog is a thick mist

indicators.note: around says the stealing word wraps the resources

parts.note: lifting is slang for stealing, theft
ores are natural mineral resources

explanation.surface: An oak tree's family stands over a rising mist, lifting it around the natural world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns FOG into GOF in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The oak is traditionally called the monarch of the woods, a poetic title.

clue.text: Bed layer mostly churned up, ready for infusion of colour?

indicators.note: churned up says the letters are stirred into a new order
mostly means the last letter of the phrase is left off

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bed's layer, mostly churned up, is ready to be tinted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the R from BEDLAYER, and 'churned up' rearranges BEDLAYE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric that can take a tint accepts colour soaked into it.

clue.text: Mutual need to bury deep, scattered around terminal enclosure

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body

indicators.note: around says the shuffled letters go either side of the next pieces
scattered tells us the letters of the word deep are strewn into a new order

parts.note: a terminal point is an end
ENC is the abbreviation for enclosure, as on a letter

explanation.surface: Something about needing to bury something deep in scattered fashion round a final pen; it reads as a gardening instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' gives DEPE, which 'around' wraps about the other two pieces; ENC is the abbreviation written at the foot of a letter to flag an enclosed document.
explanation.definitionFit: When two parties each rely on the other, that reciprocal reliance is a shared need.

clue.text: Not all of inevitable punishment

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Not every punishment is unavoidable.
explanation.definitionFit: A monetary penalty imposed by a court is a common form of punishment.

clue.text: Perhaps canine's beginning to howl after blast

indicators.note: after places the single letter behind the word for a blast

parts.note: a toot is a short blast on a horn

indicators.note: beginning to selects the opening letter of the word howl

explanation.surface: A dog starts to howl after a horn blast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps canine' is the definition: a canine is one kind of tooth; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Canines are the pointed teeth beside the incisors, so a canine is an example of this.

clue.text: It may help to part company with doctor

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Something that might help you leave a firm, with a doctor's help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' here is the parting in one's hair, not leaving company.
explanation.definitionFit: A toothed grooming tool is what you use to make a parting in hair.

clue.text: Regular supplies from blackberry tart producer

indicators.note: regular supplies means every other letter is taken from the word

explanation.surface: A pie maker gets steady supplies of blackberries.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who bakes pastries and bread makes tarts for a living.

clue.text: Germanic settler's point of view

definitions.meaning: one of a Germanic people who settled in England in the fifth century
a particular approach or slant on a story

explanation.surface: A Germanic settler's perspective.
explanation.definitionFit: The tribe that gave England its name, and a slant or perspective on a matter.

clue.text: Regalia displayed in place for the rest of the cattle

definitions.text: place for the rest of the cattle

indicators.note: displayed suggests the regalia are laid out in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Royal regalia shown off in a place where cattle rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A holding area where livestock are rested on the way to market or slaughter.

clue.text: Girl is French and in French city mostly

indicators.note: in places the conjunction inside the shortened city name
mostly means the final letter of the city is dropped

parts.note: Nantes is a city in western France
et is the French word for and

explanation.surface: A girl turns out to be French and living in a French city.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's given name, familiar from the musical No, No, Nanette.

clue.text: Poles on benefit holding mass in stone tombs

indicators.note: on places the second piece after the first in this across clue
holding means the benefit word wraps round the single letter

parts.note: the dole is British slang for unemployment benefit
M is the physics symbol for mass
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: People of Poland claiming benefit hold a Mass among stone tombs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' are not people from Poland but the two compass poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Prehistoric megalithic structures of upright stones and a capstone, thought to be burial chambers.

clue.text: Condemned credit interest's introduction in legal document

indicators.note: in places the letters within the legal document

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

indicators.note: introduction picks the opening letter of the word interest

explanation.surface: A legal document condemning the introduction of interest on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: To condemn is to denounce publicly, to criticise strongly.

clue.text: Sandwich-ready, maybe holding last of tofu, thoroughly rinsed

indicators.note: holding says the bread word wraps the single letter

parts.note: bread cut into pieces ready for sandwiches is sliced, one example

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of tofu

explanation.surface: A sandwich prepared with tofu, washed thoroughly.
explanation.definitionFit: To flush something with a strong flow of water is to rinse it thoroughly.

clue.text: Sun and Express having a reasonable balance?

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
to vent feelings is to express them

explanation.surface: Two tabloid newspapers, the Sun and the Express, are financially sound.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun and the Daily Express are British tabloid newspapers, which the surface invokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or firm able to pay their debts has money left over, a healthy bank balance.

clue.text: Small hollow needs internal massage to prepare for operation

indicators.note: internal says the massage word sits inside the hollow

parts.note: a cup is a hollow
to rub is to massage

explanation.surface: A small dip needs a massage inside before surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons wash hands and arms thoroughly before operating.

clue.text: Chief of the senses in which government is undermined

indicators.note: chief of takes the leading letter of the following word

parts.note: one's senses or wits are one's reason

explanation.surface: The most important of the senses lets you see government undermined.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying the state, such as plotting to overthrow it, is the crime of betrayal of one's country.

clue.text: Caught by worker, for one insincere talk

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a worker is one kind of ant, so an ant is an example

explanation.surface: An employee is caught spouting hypocritical talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypocritical, sanctimonious speech is called this, as is the jargon of a group.

clue.text: Rush spicy dish with starter made hot

indicators.note: the starter is the dish's opening letter, which is replaced by another

parts.note: a curry is a spicy dish
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Rushing out a curry, with the first course made extra hot.
explanation.definitionFit: To rush is to move or act with great haste.

clue.text: Left unfulfilled about romantic attachment

indicators.note: unfulfilled says the word is not completed, losing its final letter

parts.note: over can mean about, as in arguing over something

explanation.surface: Someone left feeling unfulfilled by a romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfulfilled' cuts the last letter from OVER, leaving OVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep affection for a romantic partner is the most common sense of the word.

clue.text: Some turbulence in cases of extended delay

indicators.note: cases are outer coverings, so the first and last letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: Turbulence on a flight with a long delay.
explanation.definitionFit: A swirl of water or air running against the main current is a small bit of turbulence.

clue.text: Tends to ignore article that may change one's view

indicators.note: to ignore says one letter is left out of the word for tends

parts.note: to lean towards is to tend to
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: People tend to ignore an article that might change their minds.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved piece of glass in spectacles or cameras alters what one sees.

clue.text: Unusually sincere builder's extreme simplicity

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters of the two words are arranged in an uncommon order

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored and the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An unusually honest builder whose work is stripped back to the basics.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the S of 'builder's' is needed in the letter pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cannot be broken down any further has the ultimate degree of simplicity.

clue.text: Unmoved doctor departs when nursing you — once, twice!

indicators.note: nursing means holding something inside, as a nurse cradles a baby

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

indicators.note: twice says the archaic pronoun is written two times

parts.note: ye is how you was once written, an archaic form

explanation.surface: A doctor leaves, unmoved, while looking after a patient who keeps repeating themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks an archaic word: YE is old English for 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who does not cry at a sad event stays emotionally untouched.

clue.text: Large vessel added to crush Afghan people

indicators.note: added to places the vessel after the crush

parts.note: a pash is a schoolgirl crush, an infatuation
a tun is a large cask for wine or beer

explanation.surface: A big ship is added to the crush of a crowd of Afghans.
explanation.walkthrough: PASH is dated British slang for an infatuation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pashtun are the largest ethnic group of Afghanistan, also living in Pakistan.
